minutes.headline: ZBA extended Amber's Pizza permit two years; Pond View 40B water/sewer authority question deferred to Jan 25 straw poll.
minutes.summary: The board granted a two-year extension for an Amber's Pizza special permit, then heard the peer-review traffic report on the 200-unit Pond View Commons 40B project, with public comment on Howard Street conditions. Town counsel and applicant's counsel proposed a stay and early Housing Appeals Committee review of the water and sewer waivers; members were split or unready, and the hearing was continued to January 25 at 8 pm for a limited discussion.

attendees.role: presenter (peer review traffic engineer, NSM Associates)

public_comment.topic: Site entrance is near the crest of a hill and a corner; heavy existing traffic on Howard Street and West Townsend Road.
Bus stop stops traffic at the narrow curve; doesn't think 200 apartments are feasible; speeding trucks.
Road width concerns and when a submission is considered complete.
Asked about minimum road width standards for Howard Street.
Road is narrow and overgrown; walkers must step off for cars and plows.
Asked why unsignalized intersections like Northfield Road were not studied and about holiday-week counts.
Concern that construction and traffic will affect well water.
Questioned where the ZBA gets authority to override a separate governmental entity, the water district.

votes.motion: Grant the Amber's Pizza special permit extension for two years for the building expansion as proposed.
votes.outcome: passed (voice vote, all in favor; count not stated)

votes.motion: Continue the Pond View 40B hearing to January 25 at 8 pm.
votes.outcome: passed (voice vote, all in favor; count not stated)

budget_items.what_was_said: The applicant declined to fund the engineering peer review until the board decides on the water and sewer waivers. Counsel said the applicant would fund reasonable reviews afterward.
The Sewer Commission letter said connection fees and a privilege fee are contractual and should not be waived. It also mentioned an infiltration and inflow requirement or fee.
figures_as_heard: four gallons of one one in II infiltration
50 percent of the most recent betterment

budget_items.what_was_said: Town counsel noted the applicant could face substantial costs for peer reviews and the plans needed for water and sewer.
Counsel noted the board earlier voted on the application fee waiver in order to get funds sooner.

decisions.decision: A straw poll on authority to waive water and sewer votes gave about three against and one unready or unstated; no formal vote taken.
Counsel will hold a limited discussion of about 30 minutes after the other hearings on Jan 25, and draft a stipulation for Feb 8 if the board lacks authority.
Hearing deadline is March 13 to close the hearing, then 40 days to decide, unless extended by agreement.
Peer reviewer suggested conditions: vegetation clearing, Hollis Road signal timing, TDM measures, and a road safety audit; applicant's counsel raised no real objection.

what_happened.line: The board continued the Pond View Commons 40B hearing to January 25 at 8 pm, with no decision yet on whether it can waive water and sewer requirements.
A straw poll on the board's authority to waive water and sewer rules leaned against, with one member unready; no formal vote was taken.

Town counsel and the applicant's counsel proposed a stay and early Housing Appeals Committee review of the water and sewer waivers; counsel will draft a stipulation for February 8 if the board lacks authority.
The board voted by voice to extend the Amber's Pizza special permit for two years for the building expansion as proposed.
The traffic peer reviewer suggested conditions including vegetation clearing, signal timing at Hollis Road, travel-demand measures and a road safety audit.

why_it_matters: Whether a state-override housing board can set aside the water district's and Sewer Commission's rules decides who controls connection terms for a 200-unit project, and the applicant has tied funding of further engineering reviews to that answer.
Residents of Howard Street and nearby wells raised road width, traffic and groundwater concerns that the board has so far taken in without a decision, and the hearing has a legal clock running.
